I'm checking whether the streaming engine's select is picking columns by position, since the IEJoin output seems to still contain y even though the plan expects it to be coalesced away. With the in-memory engine, select("x") leaks y too, which fits the idea that the kernel ignores the coalesce setting.

I'm checking whether the streaming engine's lowering of the IEJoin output matches the schema the optimizer produced, since the in-memory engine gives correct results for the same query. I'll also confirm that predicate pushdown runs before projection pushdown, because the inner join's filters are converted to an IEJoin at that stage.

I'm checking the IEJoin case: it's excluded from the coalesce upgrade because the join type isn't Inner or Left. The real suspect is the projection pushdown branch that upgrades coalescing based on left_on and right_on, which may be applied to a non-equi join where those keys don't apply.

I'm checking whether the coalesce upgrade in projection pushdown should even apply to this IEJoin, since its keys are inequalities and x and y never match. The fix probably belongs in the Join arm, gated on the join being a pure equi join rather than a helper deciding it.

I'm checking whether the IEJoin kernel ignores the coalesce setting and whether the downstream schema logic trusts it anyway, since both seem to assume the join type alone decides it. Next I'll look at the streaming lowering and the in-memory engine's handling of IEJoin.
